benchmarks.verdict: An attractively priced monitor with benefits over the competition that should be on your shortlist.

notes: Two panel camps: (1) 4th-gen Primary RGB Tandem WOLED 280Hz (GIGABYTE MO27Q28G/FO27Q28G, ASUS XG27AQWMG, LG 27GX700A-B) – brighter SDR (~330 nits full field, 1500-nit HDR claim, True Black 500) and better text than old RWBG WOLED; (2) QD-OLED 280Hz/240Hz (GIGABYTE MO27Q2A/FO27Q2/GO27Q24, MSI X28, Alienware AW2725D) – wider gamut (~108-111% DCI-P3), 250 nits/True Black 400. Samsung has no 240-280Hz 27" QHD OLED in this generation; G60SD is 360Hz (included per brief; it overlaps segment B). GO27Q24A/G and GO27Q24 are 'limited-brightness' QD-OLED tier (200/400 nits). Measured input lag (Tom's Hardware, same methodology): FO27Q2 13 ms < MO27Q28G 14 ms < AW2725D 17 ms < Samsung G6 G60SD 18 ms < XG27AQWMG 20 ms. TechSpot names Gigabyte MO27Q28GR the top 240-280Hz value pick (≈$480-499 vs XG27AQWMG $650) and AW2725D the best QD-OLED value at ~$400. Gaps: RTINGS pages did not render numeric data via WebFetch (blocked/JS) and TFTCentral/PCMonitors reviews are video-based, so no measured numbers from them; no reputable reviews found for AORUS ELITE FO27Q28G or FO27Q24G (FO27Q28G likely shares MO27Q28G's panel); no measured benchmark found for LG 27GX700A-B or MSI X28 beyond qualitative notes. KitGuru/Profesional Review used where listed sources lacked data.
